metadata.title: Squeezing Silicon to the Limit: How to Keep GPUs from Sitting Idle? | Deep Dive on AI Infra with SGLang & RadixArk
metadata.guest: Ying Sheng, Banghua Zhu, and others
metadata.guest_role: RadixArk founders/co-founders · SGLang core team · Data center expert

conclusion: While OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic race on inference chips, Silicon Valley's hottest keyword is GPU utilization — squeezing more tokens from deployed silicon instead of endlessly buying cards. The episode maps AI Infra's four layers (power, hardware, system software, orchestration), citing CMU telemetry on 756 GPUs showing ~20% execution idle and >50% wasted inference energy in some workloads; optimization is shifting up-stack. vLLM and SGLang each raised $100M+ commercial seeds; RadixArk bets RadixAttention, cache-aware scheduling, PD disaggregation, and the Miles train-infer stack can make inference engines the 'OS' linking models to chips so open weights actually become deployable tokens.
background: Silicon Valley 101 covers the inference inflection: Baseten revenue up 20x in a year, Fireworks 4x valuation in seven months, and the vLLM/SGLang 'twin stars' going commercial. Guests from RadixArk (spun out of SGLang; founder Ying Sheng ex-xAI Inference) and data-center operators discuss pushing a $4M GB200 rack from ~50% to 90%+ utilization — equivalent to gaining a free rack. Context includes mega-cap CapEx above $1T, Huang's $4T/year AI infra forecast by 2030, and Day-0 deploy needs for open models like DeepSeek V4 and Kimi K3.
important_facts: CMU 31-day telemetry on 756 GPUs (A100 through B200): ~20% execution time and ~11% energy lost to waiting; Azure Code hits 65% idle energy, Chat workloads 52%. Lower layers (power, chips) optimize on yearly cycles with diminishing returns; upper software/orchestration (vLLM, SGLang, continuous batching, PD split) can multiply throughput several-fold. A $4M GB200 rack at 50% utilization wastes ~$2M in power, depreciation, and opportunity cost — pushing to 90% equals a free rack.

SGLang targets inference tax: Agent flows repeat system prompts, forcing KV recompute. RadixAttention uses a radix tree for cross-request prefix sharing; Anthropic-style optimizations reportedly cut cost 90%. Cache-aware scheduling batches similar requests like a kitchen reusing prep for three mapo tofu orders; eviction and distributed cache-aware load balancing route to GPUs that already hold KV. Continuous batching adds 2–4x throughput; PD disaggregation matches Prefill vs Decode to optimal hardware — DeepSeek and NVIDIA Dynamo place PD split at core architecture.

RadixArk seed round includes NVIDIA, AMD, MediaTek, Databricks, plus angels like Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan and Broadcom CEO Hock Tan; SGLang is the default Day-0 benchmark for new hardware launches. Miles training framework addresses RL post-training where generation, scoring, and weight updates fight on the same GPUs; MoE routing adds train-infer alignment complexity. Goal: demote frontier labs to shared infra — open weights from DeepSeek V4, GLM-5.2, Kimi K3 still need Day-0 engines to become tokens on NVIDIA, AMD, and emerging AI chips.

mental_model.name: Four-Layer Infra × Soft/Hard Split × Inference-Tax Removal
mental_model.components: Decompose GPU idle time across power, interconnect, system software, and orchestration; separate slow hard fixes (years, ceiling near) from high-multiple soft engineering (schedulers, kernels, cache policies). In a GPU shortage, KV reuse, continuous batching, PD split, speculative decoding, low-precision formats, and train-infer co-design turn utilization into net new capacity without new silicon purchases.
mental_model.application: Diligence AI Infra bets on measurable token-cost reduction, not narrative alone. NVDA and AMD still benefit from deploy waves, but software layers like SGLang and RadixArk capture utilization alpha and become hardware evaluation gates. Agent-heavy and RAG-heavy buyers should score prefix cache hit rates plus scheduling quality; RL post-training shops need unified Miles-class train-infer stacks. Beware CapEx without software optimization when Wall Street compares AI spend to fiber overbuild cycles.

key_insights.view: The inference inflection is here; scarcity forces software to squeeze silicon.
key_insights.question: Why not everyone build chips?
key_insights.answer: Chips are costly and slow; deployed GPUs sit idle. Utilization gains equal CapEx-free capacity — Anthropic's 200+ inference engineers and Q2 profitability show software is now a frontier-lab moat.

key_insights.view: SGLang turns KV cache into a global reusable asset.
key_insights.question: How to cut 'inference tax'?
key_insights.answer: Repeated prompts/tool schemas in agents are pure waste. Radix-tree prefix sharing plus cache-aware scheduling and load balancing to GPUs with warm KV — otherwise caches don't hit; eviction retains hot system prompts and RAG docs under memory pressure.

key_insights.view: Inference engines are becoming AI's operating system.
key_insights.question: What is RadixArk betting?
key_insights.answer: Open weights ≠ deployable tokens; Day-0 multi-model, multi-chip support. Miles + SGLang closes RL post-training loops. Vision: erase frontier-lab monopoly — anyone can train and infer at the frontier.

top_investment_implications.thesis: SGLang commercial vehicle — RadixAttention, PD split, Miles train-infer unity; strategic backers include NVDA/AMD/MediaTek; positioning as inference OS layer. Early, vLLM competition; low confidence

Inference CapEx and scarcity persist; infra optimization amplifies installed-base output rather than replacing demand. SGLang Day-0 benchmarks reinforce NVDA ecosystem lock-in while software raises effective supply
